231class Action: 

232 """The names of the five CRUD actions: the ``action`` that ``authorize`` 

233 gets. A write, such as ``CREATE`` or the action of a ``write_action`` 

234 block, also passes it to ``before_action_commit`` and 

235 ``after_action_commit``. A read, ``GET_MANY`` or ``GET_ONE``, has no 

236 commit, so it reaches only ``authorize``. 

237 

238 Each view has a class ``Action`` that lists all its actions. It is this 

239 class, until a view adds actions of its own in a subclass:: 

240 

241 class PostView(fr.AsyncRestView): 

242 class Action(fr.Action): 

243 PUBLISH = "publish" 

244 

245 An ``Action`` class has only actions. An action has an UPPER_CASE name, 

246 and its value is that name in lower case. ``write_action`` takes only a 

247 value that the view's ``Action`` declares. A view with base classes that 

248 declare actions, such as a mixin, inherits from their ``Action`` classes 

249 too. 

250 """ 

251 

252 #: Read a list, as ``GET /`` does. A read has no commit. 

253 GET_MANY = "get_many" 

254 #: Read one row, as ``GET /{id}`` does. A read has no commit. 

255 GET_ONE = "get_one" 

256 #: Create a row, as ``POST /`` does. 

257 CREATE = "create" 

258 #: Update a row, as ``PATCH /{id}`` does. 

259 UPDATE = "update" 

260 #: Delete a row, as ``DELETE /{id}`` does. 

261 DELETE = "delete" 

262 

263 def __init_subclass__(cls, **kwargs: Any) -> None: 

264 super().__init_subclass__(**kwargs) 

265 for key in dir(cls): 

266 if key.startswith("_"): 

267 continue 

268 if not key.isupper(): 

269 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

270 f"{cls.__qualname__}.{key}: an Action class has only " 

271 "actions, and an action has an UPPER_CASE name, such as " 

272 "PUBLISH = 'publish'." 

273 ) 

274 value = getattr(cls, key) 

275 if value != key.lower(): 

276 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

277 f"{cls.__qualname__}.{key} is {value!r}. The value of an " 

278 f"action is its name in lower case: {key} = {key.lower()!r}." 

279 )

290def _accepts_init_kwarg(model_cls: type, attr_name: str) -> bool: 

291 """Return True if attr_name can be passed as a keyword argument to model_cls.__init__. 

292 

293 Non-dataclass models (DeclarativeBase subclasses using mapped_column) accept all 

294 kwargs. Dataclass-based models may have fields with init=False, in which case 

295 passing the attribute to __init__ raises TypeError. 

296 """ 

297 if not dataclasses.is_dataclass(model_cls): 

298 return True 

299 dc_fields = {f.name: f for f in dataclasses.fields(model_cls)} 

300 return attr_name not in dc_fields or dc_fields[attr_name].init 

301 

302 

303def _requires_init_kwarg(model_cls: type, attr_name: str) -> bool: 

304 if not dataclasses.is_dataclass(model_cls): 

305 return False 

306 dc_fields = {f.name: f for f in dataclasses.fields(model_cls)} 

307 field = dc_fields.get(attr_name) 

308 if field is None or not field.init: 

309 return False 

310 return ( 

311 field.default is dataclasses.MISSING 

312 and field.default_factory is dataclasses.MISSING 

313 )

398def _relationship_name_for_fk(model_cls: type[Any], fk_attr_name: str) -> str | None: 

399 """Reverse of :func:`_get_unambiguous_local_fk_name`. 

400 

401 Given a scalar FK column's attribute name, return the single many-to-one 

402 relationship that uses it as its local column, or ``None`` when there is no 

403 such relationship or more than one (ambiguous, so no pairing is guessed). 

404 This is how a FK reference field finds its partner relationship without 

405 relying on the ``<relation>_id`` naming convention. 

406 """ 

407 try: 

408 mapper = sa_inspect(model_cls) 

409 except Exception: 

410 return None 

411 fk_column = mapper.columns.get(fk_attr_name) 

412 if fk_column is None: 412 ↛ 413line 412 didn't jump to line 413 because the condition on line 412 was never true

413 return None 

414 # Match by Column identity, not by ``.key``: the column's key is the DB name, 

415 # which differs from ``fk_attr_name`` under ``mapped_column("db_name", ...)``. 

416 # (``is`` also avoids ``Column.__eq__``'s SQL-expression overload.) 

417 matches = [ 

418 relationship_property.key 

419 for relationship_property in mapper.relationships 

420 if getattr(relationship_property.direction, "name", None) == "MANYTOONE" 

421 and any(column is fk_column for column in relationship_property.local_columns) 

422 ] 

423 return matches[0] if len(matches) == 1 else None

473def _json_ready(model_cls: type[Any], field_name: str, value: Any) -> Any: 

474 """Dump pydantic models on their way into a JSON column. 

475 

476 A schema field typed as a nested model validates to a model instance, and 

477 a JSON column binds through ``json.dumps``, which cannot take one. Restly 

478 owns the schema-to-model translation, so it does the dump here rather than 

479 letting the driver fail at flush with the model in the bind parameters. 

480 """ 

481 holds_model = isinstance(value, pydantic.BaseModel) or ( 

482 isinstance(value, list | tuple) 

483 and any(isinstance(item, pydantic.BaseModel) for item in value) 

484 ) 

485 if not holds_model or not _is_json_column(model_cls, field_name): 

486 return value 

487 _reject_excluded_json_fields(value, f"{model_cls.__name__}.{field_name}") 

488 return _json_data(value)

491def _column_ready( 

492 model_cls: type[Any], 

493 schema_cls: type[pydantic.BaseModel], 

494 field_name: str, 

495 value: Any, 

496) -> Any: 

497 """A value in the form of its column, by the rule of ``column_value``: a 

498 time gets the form of its column, and a number or a text must fit it. 

499 The column stores the value, so text must also fit its length. 

500 

501 A field without a column keeps its value. 

502 

503 :raises RequestValidationError: the value does not fit the column, such as 

504 a time out of range in UTC, or a number out of the range of an 

505 ``Integer``. The error has the form of a field's validation error, as 

506 ``fr.UTCDatetime`` gives it.

509 return value 

510 mapper = sa_inspect(model_cls, raiseerr=False) 

511 column = None if mapper is None else mapper.columns.get(field_name) 

512 if column is None: 

513 return value 

514 try: 

515 return column_value(column.type, value, stored=True) 

516 except ValueError as exc: 

517 field = schema_cls.model_fields.get(field_name) 

518 key = field_name if field is None else _client_name(field_name, field) 

519 raise RequestValidationError( 

520 [ 

521 { 

522 "type": "value_error", 

523 "loc": ("body", key), 

524 "msg": value_error_reason(exc), 

525 "input": value, 

526 "ctx": {"error": exc}, 

527 } 

528 ] 

529 ) from None

532def _reject_excluded_json_fields(value: Any, column: str) -> None: 

533 """Reject exclusions, secrets, and document values that cannot be 

534 inspected safely. A JSON dump leaves out an excluded field and masks a 

535 secret, so the column would not get the value.""" 

536 pending = [value] 

537 seen: set[int] = set() 

538 while pending: 

539 item = pending.pop() 

540 if dataclasses.is_dataclass(item) or isinstance(item, Iterator): 

541 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

542 f"{column}: documents containing dataclasses or iterators cannot " 

543 "be stored automatically in a plain JSON column. Use a SQLAlchemy " 

544 "TypeDecorator to define their storage representation." 

545 ) 

546 if isinstance(item, _SECRET_TYPES): 

547 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

548 f"{column}: the document holds a secret, such as a SecretStr. A " 

549 "JSON dump masks a secret, so documents with secrets cannot be " 

550 "stored automatically in a plain JSON column. Use a SQLAlchemy " 

551 "TypeDecorator to define their storage representation." 

552 ) 

553 if isinstance(item, str | bytes | bytearray) or not isinstance( 

554 item, (pydantic.BaseModel, Mapping, Sequence, Set, Enum) 

555 ): 

556 continue 

557 if id(item) in seen: 557 ↛ 558line 557 didn't jump to line 558 because the condition on line 557 was never true

558 continue 

559 seen.add(id(item)) 

560 if isinstance(item, pydantic.BaseModel): 

561 for name, field in type(item).model_fields.items(): 

562 if field.exclude: 

563 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

564 f"{column}: {type(item).__name__}.{name} is excluded from " 

565 "serialization. Documents with WriteOnly or " 

566 "Field(exclude=True) fields cannot be stored automatically " 

567 "in a plain JSON column. Use a SQLAlchemy TypeDecorator " 

568 "to define their storage representation." 

569 ) 

570 # A secret field, also one without a value yet: the first 

571 # write of such a document fails, not the first with a secret. 

572 if _hides_value(field): 

573 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

574 f"{column}: {type(item).__name__}.{name} has a secret " 

575 "type, such as SecretStr, which a JSON dump masks. " 

576 "Documents with secret fields cannot be stored " 

577 "automatically in a plain JSON column. Use a SQLAlchemy " 

578 "TypeDecorator to define their storage representation." 

579 ) 

580 pending.append(getattr(item, name, None)) 

581 if item.model_extra: 

582 pending.extend(item.model_extra.values()) 

583 elif isinstance(item, Mapping): 

584 pending.extend(item.keys()) 

585 pending.extend(item.values()) 

586 elif isinstance(item, Enum): 

587 pending.append(item.value) 

588 else: 

589 pending.extend(item)

1117class View:

1119 Class-based view primitive for FastAPI. 

1120 

1121 Group related endpoints on a class, share dependencies and metadata via 

1122 class attributes, and let subclasses override individual route methods. 

1123 Routes are bound at :func:`include_view` time, not at class-definition 

1124 time, so subclassing works the way Python developers expect: override a 

1125 method on a subclass and the override is what runs. 

1126 

1127 Most users will subclass :class:`RestView` or :class:`AsyncRestView`, 

1128 which extend ``View`` with CRUD scaffolding. Use ``View`` directly for 

1129 grouped non-CRUD endpoints (auth flows, custom RPC routes, etc.). 

1130 """ 

1131 

1132 #: The URL prefix of every route. Each class in the hierarchy that sets one 

1133 #: adds a segment, base first. Without a prefix, the routes are at the root.

1167 if sys.version_info >= (3, 14): 1167 ↛ 1168line 1167 didn't jump to line 1168 because the condition on line 1167 was never true

1174def _setting_names(view_cls: type) -> dict[str, type]: 

1175 """The view settings of ``view_cls``, with the Restly class that declares 

1176 each. A setting is a ``ClassVar`` of Restly's view classes, such as 

1177 ``tags`` or ``model``: Restly reads it from the class.""" 

1178 settings: dict[str, type] = {} 

1179 for klass in reversed(view_cls.__mro__): 

1180 if not klass.__module__.startswith("fastapi_restly."): 

1181 continue 

1182 for name, annotation in _own_annotations(klass).items(): 

1183 if get_origin(annotation) is not ClassVar or name.startswith("_"): 

1184 continue 

1185 # a private class that declares the setting again, such as a 

1186 # mixin, is no name for a message 

1187 if name not in settings or not klass.__name__.startswith("_"): 

1188 settings[name] = klass 

1189 return settings

1192def _reject_route_names_of_settings(view_cls: type) -> None: 

1193 """Refuse a route method with the name of a view setting, also from a 

1194 mixin. A method is a class attribute too, so it would replace the 

1195 setting. A class may still set the setting over a route of a mixin.""" 

1196 for name, declarer in _setting_names(view_cls).items(): 

1197 if hasattr(inspect.getattr_static(view_cls, name, None), "_api_route_args"): 

1198 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1199 f"{view_cls.__name__}.{name}(){_set_by(view_cls, name)} is a " 

1200 f"route method with the name of the view setting " 

1201 f"{declarer.__name__}.{name}, so it replaces the setting. Give " 

1202 f"the method another name. The route keeps its path." 

1203 )

1207#: must not be named like one of these: it would shadow the verb (which the 

1208#: ``handle_<verb>`` handlers call) and collide with ``<verb>_endpoint`` at the 

1209#: same path. Override the business method *without* a decorator for domain 

1210#: logic; use ``<verb>_endpoint`` or a distinct name for a custom route. 

1211#: ``get_one`` and ``get_many`` are final, so the class-definition guard 

1212#: refuses them first. A plain ``View`` has none of these methods, so the 

1213#: names are free there. 

1214_BARE_VERB_NAMES = ("create", "update", "delete")

1266 _init_view_cls_and_add_to_router(view_cls, parent_router)

1276def route(path: str, **api_route_kwargs: Any) -> Callable[..., Any]:

1281 ``APIRouter.add_api_route()`` when :func:`include_view` registers the 

1282 view. Without ``methods=``, the route is a ``GET`` with status 200, as in 

1283 FastAPI. :func:`get`, :func:`post`, :func:`patch`, :func:`put` and 

1284 :func:`delete` set the method and the status code for you. 

1285 """ 

1286

1288 # Create a new attribute: '_api_route_args' 

1289 func._api_route_args = (path, api_route_kwargs) # type: ignore[attr-defined] 

1290 return func 

1291 

1292 return store_args_decorator

1298def list_filter(key: str) -> Callable[[_F], _F]: 

1299 """Make a view method the filter for the query key ``key``. 

1300 

1301 For a filter that the generated keys do not give:: 

1302 

1303 @fr.list_filter("popular") 

1304 def filter_popular(self, value: bool) -> ColumnElement[bool]: 

1305 popular = Item.view_count > 1000 

1306 return popular if value else ~popular 

1307 

1308 The method takes one value after ``self``. Its type becomes the type of 

1309 the key in the list params, so OpenAPI shows it and a bad value gets 

1310 ``422``. The docstring becomes the description of the key. Without a 

1311 default, the view calls the method when the key has a value. With a 

1312 default, it calls the method on every list request, with the default 

1313 when the key is missing. 

1314 

1315 The method returns a SQLAlchemy condition, a clause or ``None`` for no 

1316 condition. The view adds it to the statement with AND, inside the scope. 

1317 The condition may use only the tables that are in the statement; use a 

1318 relationship (``.has()``/``.any()``) for another table. On an async view 

1319 the method can be ``async def``. 

1320 

1321 The key is a name of your own, such as ``popular``, or a field and an 

1322 operator, such as ``name__length``. The operator may be one that Restly 

1323 generates for other fields, or a new one. Before the last ``__`` comes a 

1324 field with filters, as in the generated keys, such as ``vendor.name``. 

1325 

1326 The key is always on: ``include_filters`` and ``exclude_filters`` choose 

1327 among the generated keys only. A subclass drops the key by setting the 

1328 method name to ``None``. 

1329 

1330 :raises RestlyConfigurationError: ``key`` is not a non-empty string, 

1331 starts with ``_``, is the name of a Pydantic model attribute, or has 

1332 ``__`` without one field before it and one operator without ``.`` 

1333 after it. A key that is a page parameter, the 

1334 sort parameter or a generated key that is on fails when the view 

1335 registers, and so does a key with ``__`` or ``.`` that does not start 

1336 with a field with filters. 

1337 """ 

1338 _check_own_key_name(key) 

1339 

1340 def mark(method: _F) -> _F: 

1341 method._fr_list_filter = key # type: ignore[attr-defined] 

1342 return method 

1343 

1344 return mark 

1345 

1346 

1347def _check_own_key_name(key: Any) -> None: 

1348 """Reject a key that cannot be a query parameter of the list params. 

1349 

1350 The last ``__`` splits a field from an operator, as in the generated 

1351 keys. The view checks the field when it registers. 

1352 """ 

1353 if not isinstance(key, str) or not key: 

1354 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1355 f"@fr.list_filter needs a key as a non-empty string, got {key!r}." 

1356 ) 

1357 field, separator, operator = key.rpartition("__") 

1358 if separator and "." in operator: 

1359 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1360 f"@fr.list_filter({key!r}): an operator has no '.'. A '.' goes in " 

1361 "the field, as in 'vendor.name__startswith'." 

1362 ) 

1363 if separator and (not field or not operator or "__" in field): 

1364 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1365 f"@fr.list_filter({key!r}): '__' splits a field from an operator, " 

1366 "as in 'name__startswith'. Write it once, with a field before it " 

1367 "and an operator after it." 

1368 ) 

1369 # the list params are a Pydantic model with one field per key 

1370 if key.startswith("_") or hasattr(pydantic.BaseModel, key): 

1371 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1372 f"@fr.list_filter({key!r}): a key cannot start with '_' or be " 

1373 "the name of a Pydantic model attribute." 

1374 ) 

1375 

1376 

1377def _list_filter_methods(cls: type) -> dict[str, Any]: 

1378 """The methods of ``cls`` with ``@fr.list_filter``, by name, in the 

1379 order that the classes define them. 

1380 

1381 A name set to ``None`` drops the filter of a base class. 

1382 

1383 :raises RestlyConfigurationError: a method overrides a filter method 

1384 without the decorator. 

1385 """ 

1386 names: dict[str, None] = {} 

1387 for klass in reversed(cls.__mro__): 

1388 names.update(dict.fromkeys(vars(klass))) 

1389 methods: dict[str, Any] = {} 

1390 for name in names: 

1391 marked = [ 

1392 klass 

1393 for klass in cls.__mro__ 

1394 if hasattr(vars(klass).get(name), "_fr_list_filter") 

1395 ] 

1396 if not marked: 

1397 continue 

1398 value = inspect.getattr_static(cls, name) 

1399 if value is None: 

1400 continue 

1401 if not hasattr(value, "_fr_list_filter"): 

1402 key = getattr(vars(marked[0])[name], "_fr_list_filter") 

1403 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1404 f"{cls.__name__}.{name}{_set_by(cls, name)} overrides the " 

1405 f"filter method of {marked[0].__name__} without " 

1406 f"@fr.list_filter. Add @fr.list_filter({key!r}) to keep the " 

1407 f"key, or set {name} = None to drop it." 

1408 ) 

1409 methods[name] = value 

1410 return methods 

1411 

1412 

1413def _own_filters(cls: type) -> list[_OwnFilter]: 

1414 """The own filter keys of a view, with the types of their values. 

1415 

1416 :raises RestlyConfigurationError: two methods have one key, or a method 

1417 does not take one value with a type. 

1418 """ 

1419 filters: list[_OwnFilter] = [] 

1420 method_of: dict[str, str] = {} 

1421 for name, method in _list_filter_methods(cls).items(): 

1422 label = f"{cls.__name__}.{name}" 

1423 key = method._fr_list_filter 

1424 if key in method_of: 

1425 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1426 f"{cls.__name__}: {method_of[key]} and {name} are both the " 

1427 f"filter for the key {key!r}." 

1428 ) 

1429 method_of[key] = name 

1430 parameters = list(_route_parameters(method).values())[1:] 

1431 if len(parameters) != 1 or parameters[0].kind not in ( 

1432 inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_ONLY, 

1433 inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD, 

1434 ): 

1435 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1436 f"{label} must take one value after self, as in " 

1437 f"'def {name}(self, value: bool)'." 

1438 ) 

1439 parameter = parameters[0] 

1440 if parameter.annotation is inspect.Parameter.empty: 

1441 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1442 f"{label} needs a type on {parameter.name!r}, such as " 

1443 f"'{parameter.name}: bool'. The type checks the value from the " 

1444 "URL, and OpenAPI shows it." 

1445 ) 

1446 # Only the value's type is evaluated: the return type may name a 

1447 # class that the module imports under TYPE_CHECKING. 

1448 holder = types.SimpleNamespace( 

1449 __annotations__={parameter.name: parameter.annotation} 

1450 ) 

1451 try: 

1452 annotation = get_type_hints( 

1453 holder, 

1454 globalns=getattr(inspect.unwrap(method), "__globals__", {}), 

1455 include_extras=True, 

1456 )[parameter.name] 

1457 except NameError as exc: 

1458 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1459 f"{label}: the type of {parameter.name!r} cannot be resolved: {exc}." 

1460 ) from exc 

1461 filters.append( 

1462 _OwnFilter( 

1463 key=key, 

1464 method=name, 

1465 annotation=annotation, 

1466 default=( 

1467 _NO_DEFAULT 

1468 if parameter.default is inspect.Parameter.empty 

1469 else parameter.default 

1470 ), 

1471 description=inspect.getdoc(method), 

1472 ) 

1473 ) 

1474 return filters 

1475 

1476 

1477def _apply_own_filters( 

1478 stmt: Select[Any], results: Iterable[tuple[str, Any]] 

1479) -> Select[Any]: 

1480 """Add what the filter methods returned to ``stmt``, with AND. 

1481 

1482 :param results: The label of each method, such as 

1483 ``ItemView.filter_popular``, and what the method returned. 

1484 

1485 :raises TypeError: a method returned anything other than a condition, 

1486 a clause or ``None``, or a condition on a table that is not in the 

1487 statement. 

1488 """ 

1489 conditions: list[ColumnElement[bool]] = [] 

1490 for label, result in results: 

1491 if result is None or result is UNSCOPED: 

1492 continue 

1493 result = _clause_element(result) 

1494 if isinstance(result, ColumnElement): 

1495 # applying it as a clause fills members such as Current.user_id 

1496 result = where_clause(result) 

1497 if type(result) is bool: 

1498 raise TypeError( 

1499 f"{label} returned a bool, not a SQL expression. A comparison " 

1500 "on an instance attribute is a bool; compare the column " 

1501 "instead (Item.name == value)." 

1502 ) 

1503 if not isinstance(result, WhereClause): 

1504 raise TypeError( 

1505 f"{label} must return a SQLAlchemy boolean expression, a " 

1506 f"clause or None, got {type(result).__name__}." 

1507 ) 

1508 condition = result() 

1509 # a table outside the statement would be a cross join that the scope 

1510 # does not reach 

1511 try: 

1512 _guard_statement_tables(stmt, [condition]) 

1513 except TypeError as exc: 

1514 raise TypeError(f"{label}: {exc}") from None 

1515 conditions.append(condition) 

1516 return stmt.where(*conditions) if conditions else stmt 

1517

1601_FINAL_HANDLERS = ( 

1602 "handle_get_many",

1612_FINAL_LOADS = { 

1613 "get_one": ( 

1614 "get_one is the load of every item route: GET, PATCH, DELETE and "

1616 "the row by another key, such as a slug, override where_id(id). To " 

1617 "change the 404, override not_found(id). To load more relationships " 

1618 "or a SQL expression, override get_loader_options. To add a value to " 

1619 "the response, override to_single_response. To read from another " 

1620 "source on one route, replace get_one_endpoint." 

1621 ), 

1622 "get_many": ( 

1623 "get_many is the load of the list. It applies the scope, the list " 

1624 "params, the page and the count. To filter, sort or page in another " 

1625 "way, override apply_list_params, or add a filter with " 

1626 "fr.list_filter. To load more relationships or a SQL expression, " 

1627 "override get_loader_options. To add a value to each row, override " 

1628 "to_single_response. To read from another source, replace " 

1629 "get_many_endpoint." 

1630 ), 

1631 "select": ( 

1632 "select is the start of every read: select(model), the scope and the "

1637# Hooks that the loads call. A value with one of these names, such as a 

1638# text, would fail only at the first read. 

1639_LOAD_HOOKS = ("where_id", "not_found") 

1640_WRITE_VERBS = ("create", "update", "delete")

1642 

1643#: The routes that load one row by the id in the path. 

1644_ITEM_ROUTES = ("get_one_endpoint", "update_endpoint", "delete_endpoint", "put")

1647def _check_composite_key(cls: Any) -> None: 

1648 """Refuse item routes on a model with a composite primary key and the 

1649 default ``where_id``: an id from the path cannot name one row.""" 

1650 if len(sa_inspect(cls.model).primary_key) < 2: 

1651 return 

1652 if getattr(cls.where_id, "__module__", "").startswith("fastapi_restly."): 

1653 routes = [name for name in _ITEM_ROUTES if _serves_route(cls, name)] 

1654 if routes: 

1655 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1656 f"{cls.__name__}: {cls.model.__name__} has a composite primary " 

1657 f"key, so an id from the path cannot name one row, and the " 

1658 f"item routes ({', '.join(routes)}) need it. Set " 

1659 "id_type = str, and override where_id(id): split the id, and " 

1660 "return sqlalchemy.and_(Model.a == a, Model.b == b). Or leave " 

1661 "the item routes out with include_routes or exclude_routes." 

1662 ) 

1663 

1664 

1665def _check_load_hooks(cls: type) -> None: 

1666 """Refuse a load hook that the loads cannot call. 

1667 

1668 ``where_id`` builds SQL, so it is never ``async``. ``not_found`` may be 

1669 ``async`` on an async view, which awaits it, but not on a sync one. 

1670 """ 

1671 is_async = getattr(cls, "_fr_async_view", False) 

1672 for klass in cls.__mro__: 

1673 if klass.__module__.startswith("fastapi_restly."): 

1674 continue 

1675 origin = _origin(cls, klass) 

1676 for name in _LOAD_HOOKS: 

1677 if name not in vars(klass): 

1678 continue 

1679 # through the descriptor: a classmethod or a staticmethod is 

1680 # callable once it is looked up 

1681 hook = getattr(klass, name) 

1682 if not callable(hook): 

1683 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1684 f"{cls.__name__}.{name}{origin} is a " 

1685 f"{type(vars(klass)[name]).__name__}, but the loads call " 

1686 f"{name}(id). " 

1687 f"Define {name} as a method, or use another name for the " 

1688 "value." 

1689 ) 

1690 if inspect.iscoroutinefunction(hook) and ( 

1691 name == "where_id" or not is_async 

1692 ): 

1693 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1694 f"{cls.__name__}.{name}{origin} is async, but " 

1695 + ( 

1696 "where_id builds SQL, so it runs no query. Define it with def." 

1697 if name == "where_id" 

1698 else "a sync view cannot await it. Define it with def." 

1699 ) 

1700 ) 

1701 

1702 

1703def _check_actions(cls: type) -> None: 

1704 """Refuse a view whose ``Action`` does not inherit from the ``Action`` of 

1705 a base class. 

1706 

1707 Each class that declares ``Action`` adds actions, and a view's ``Action`` 

1708 must have all of them: the view's own class, or a mixin's, or two bases 

1709 that each declare one, where Python takes the first and drops the other. 

1710 """ 

1711 action = cls.Action # type: ignore[attr-defined] 

1712 declared: list[tuple[type, Any]] = [] 

1713 for klass in cls.__mro__: 

1714 if "Action" not in vars(klass): 

1715 continue 

1716 value = vars(klass)["Action"] 

1717 if all(value is not seen for _, seen in declared): 

1718 declared.append((klass, value)) 

1719 for klass, value in declared: 

1720 if not (isinstance(value, type) and issubclass(value, Action)): 

1721 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1722 f"{cls.__name__}.Action{_origin(cls, klass)} does not inherit " 

1723 "from fr.Action. Declare it as class Action(fr.Action)." 

1724 ) 

1725 missing = [ 

1726 (klass, base) for klass, base in declared if not issubclass(action, base) 

1727 ] 

1728 if not missing: 

1729 return 

1730 # the classes to inherit from: the bases' Action classes, without one 

1731 # that another of them already inherits from 

1732 bases = [(klass, base) for klass, base in declared if klass is not cls] 

1733 keep = [ 

1734 _action_class_name(klass, base) 

1735 for klass, base in bases 

1736 if not any(other is not base and issubclass(other, base) for _, other in bases) 

1737 ] 

1738 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1739 f"{cls.__name__}.Action{_set_by(cls, 'Action')} does not inherit from " 

1740 f"{', '.join(_action_class_name(klass, base) for klass, base in missing)}. " 

1741 "A view's Action has all the actions of its bases. " 

1742 f"Declare it on {cls.__name__} with every base: " 

1743 f"class Action({', '.join(keep)})." 

1744 ) 

1745 

1746 

1747def _action_class_name(klass: type, action: type) -> str: 

1748 """How a message names the ``Action`` that ``klass`` declares.""" 

1749 return "fr.Action" if action is Action else f"{klass.__name__}.Action" 

1750 

1751 

1752def _check_action_name(view: Any, action: Any) -> None: 

1753 """Raise ``ValueError`` when ``write_action`` gets an action that the 

1754 view's ``Action`` does not declare.""" 

1755 if _declares(type(view).Action, action): 

1756 return 

1757 name = type(view).__name__ 

1758 raise ValueError( 

1759 f"{name}.write_action({action!r}, ...): unknown action {action!r}. " 

1760 f"{name}.Action does not declare it." 

1761 ) 

1762 

1763 

1764def _final_handler_message(view_name: str, name: str, origin: str) -> str: 

1765 """What a subclass that defines ``name`` is told to use instead.""" 

1766 verb = name.removeprefix("handle_") 

1767 if verb not in _WRITE_VERBS: 

1768 return ( 

1769 f"{view_name} defines {name}{origin}, which is a final handler: it " 

1770 "handles the steps of the request, and a custom route calls it. " 

1771 "Put a gate in authorize, the rows in scope, the lookup of an id " 

1772 "in where_id, the list params in apply_list_params, a response " 

1773 f"value in to_single_response, and the HTTP contract in " 

1774 f"{verb}_endpoint." 

1775 ) 

1776 return ( 

1777 f"{view_name} defines {name}{origin}, which is a final handler: it " 

1778 f"handles the steps of the request, and a custom route calls it. Put " 

1779 f"domain logic in the {verb} business method, a gate in authorize, " 

1780 "a side effect in before_action_commit or after_action_commit, " 

1781 f"and the HTTP contract in {verb}_endpoint. To put several writes in " 

1782 f"one commit, call {name} inside shared_write_action_commit()." 

1783 )

1786# Replaced by ``pagination``. A view that still sets one is told what to write. 

1787_REPLACED_PAGINATION_SETTINGS = ("paginated", "default_page_size", "max_page_size")

1790def _replaced_pagination_message( 

1791 view_name: str, found: dict[str, tuple[Any, str]] 

1792) -> str: 

1793 """What a view that sets old pagination settings writes instead: one 

1794 suggestion that carries every value it set. ``found`` maps each setting 

1795 to its value and where it came from.""" 

1796 values = {name: value for name, (value, _) in found.items()} 

1797 sizes = { 

1798 name: values[name] 

1799 for name in ("default_page_size", "max_page_size") 

1800 if name in values 

1801 } 

1802 maximum = sizes.get("max_page_size") 

1803 if ( 

1804 "default_page_size" not in sizes 

1805 and isinstance(maximum, int) 

1806 and maximum < DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE 

1807 ): 

1808 # the default page size of 50 would be above the new maximum 

1809 sizes = {"default_page_size": maximum, **sizes} 

1810 if values.get("paginated") is False: 

1811 instead = "Write 'pagination = None' to return every row." 

1812 elif sizes: 

1813 arguments = ", ".join(f"{name}={value!r}" for name, value in sizes.items()) 

1814 instead = ( 

1815 f"Write 'pagination = fr.NumberedPagination({arguments})', or call " 

1816 f"'.replace({arguments})' on pagination settings that views share." 

1817 ) 

1818 if "paginated" in values: 1818 ↛ 1819line 1818 didn't jump to line 1819 because the condition on line 1818 was never true

1819 instead += " Remove 'paginated': views paginate by default." 

1820 else: 

1821 instead = "Remove it: views paginate by default." 

1822 names = ", ".join(f"{name}{origin}" for name, (_, origin) in found.items()) 

1823 verb = "was" if len(found) == 1 else "were" 

1824 return ( 

1825 f"{view_name} sets {names}, which {verb} replaced by the 'pagination' " 

1826 f"setting. {instead}" 

1827 ) 

1828 

1829 

1830def _check_pagination_setting(cls: type) -> None: 

1831 """Reject the replaced pagination settings, and a ``pagination`` that is 

1832 not a settings instance. Runs when the class is defined and again at 

1833 registration, so a value assigned to the class later is caught too.""" 

1834 # the old settings are no longer read; a definition would be silently 

1835 # dead, and a dead max_page_size is a cap that is gone 

1836 found: dict[str, tuple[Any, str]] = {} 

1837 for klass in cls.__mro__: 

1838 for name in _REPLACED_PAGINATION_SETTINGS: 

1839 if name in vars(klass) and name not in found: 

1840 origin = _origin(cls, klass) 

1841 found[name] = (vars(klass)[name], origin) 

1842 if found: 

1843 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1844 _replaced_pagination_message(cls.__name__, found) 

1845 ) 

1846 pagination = getattr(cls, "pagination", None) 

1847 if not ( 

1848 pagination is None or isinstance(pagination, (NumberedPagination, NoPagination)) 

1849 ): 

1850 hint = ( 

1851 f" Create an instance: fr.{pagination.__name__}()." 

1852 if pagination in (NumberedPagination, NoPagination) 

1853 else "" 

1854 ) 

1855 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1856 f"{cls.__name__}.pagination must be a fr.NumberedPagination or " 

1857 f"fr.NoPagination instance, or None, got {pagination!r}.{hint}" 

1858 )

1861def _check_list_settings(cls: type) -> None: 

1862 """Reject a list setting with a bad value, when the class is defined: a 

1863 key setting that is not a tuple of keys and patterns, a sort parameter 

1864 name that cannot be a query parameter, a ``default_sort`` that is not 

1865 sort keys, or a ``sort_nulls`` that is not ``'first'``, ``'last'`` or 

1866 ``None``. Whether each key matches a field is checked when the view 

1867 registers, with the schema.""" 

1868 for name in _KEY_SETTINGS: 

1869 if name in vars(cls): 

1870 _check_key_setting(f"{cls.__name__}.{name}", vars(cls)[name]) 

1871 if "sort_query_param" in vars(cls): 

1872 _check_query_param( 

1873 f"{cls.__name__}.sort_query_param", vars(cls)["sort_query_param"] 

1874 ) 

1875 if "default_sort" in vars(cls): 

1876 _check_default_sort(f"{cls.__name__}.default_sort", vars(cls)["default_sort"]) 

1877 # also a value from a mixin, which nothing else checks 

1878 sort_nulls = getattr(cls, "sort_nulls", "last") 

1879 if sort_nulls not in ("first", "last", None): 

1880 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1881 f"{cls.__name__}.sort_nulls{_set_by(cls, 'sort_nulls')} must be " 

1882 f"'first', 'last' or None, got {sort_nulls!r}." 

1883 ) 

1884 

1885 

1886def _check_unknown_query_params(cls: type) -> None: 

1887 value = vars(cls).get("unknown_query_params", "forbid") 

1888 if value not in ("forbid", "ignore"): 

1889 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1890 f"{cls.__name__}.unknown_query_params must be 'forbid' or 'ignore', " 

1891 f"got {value!r}." 

1892 )

1895#: The view settings that Restly generates the list params with, besides 

1896#: the pagination, and their defaults. 

1897_LIST_SETTING_DEFAULTS: dict[str, Any] = { 

1898 **_KEY_SETTING_DEFAULTS, 

1899 "sort_query_param": _SORT_QUERY_PARAM, 

1900 "default_sort": None, 

1901}

1904def _list_setting(cls: type, name: str) -> Any: 

1905 """The value of a list setting of a view, as it is recorded. 

1906 

1907 :raises RestlyConfigurationError: a key setting is not keys, or a 

1908 ``default_sort`` is not sort keys, such as one that a mixin sets, 

1909 which is not checked when it is defined. 

1910 """ 

1911 value = getattr(cls, name) 

1912 label = f"{cls.__name__}.{name}{_set_by(cls, name)}" 

1913 if name == "sort_query_param": 

1914 return value 

1915 if name == "default_sort": 

1916 _check_default_sort(label, value) 

1917 return value 

1918 return _check_key_setting(label, value) 

1919 

1920 

1921#: The list methods that an async view awaits, and a sync view calls. 

1922_LIST_METHODS = ("apply_list_params", "apply_filters") 

1923 

1924 

1925def _check_list_methods(cls: type, *, is_async: bool) -> None: 

1926 """Reject a list method of the wrong kind when the class is defined. 

1927 

1928 An async view awaits :meth:`apply_list_params` and :meth:`apply_filters`, 

1929 so a plain ``def`` fails there on the first request, and a sync view 

1930 would get a coroutine instead of a statement. A sync view also calls its 

1931 filter methods without await. A filter method that is overridden 

1932 without ``@fr.list_filter`` fails here too. 

1933 """ 

1934 filter_methods = _list_filter_methods(cls) 

1935 if not is_async: 

1936 for name, method in filter_methods.items(): 

1937 if inspect.iscoroutinefunction(method): 

1938 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1939 f"{cls.__name__}.{name}{_set_by(cls, name)} is 'async " 

1940 "def', but a sync view calls it without await. Write " 

1941 f"'def {name}', or use fr.AsyncRestView." 

1942 ) 

1943 for name in _LIST_METHODS: 

1944 method = getattr(cls, name, None) 

1945 if method is None or inspect.iscoroutinefunction(method) == is_async: 

1946 continue 

1947 origin = _set_by(cls, name) 

1948 if is_async: 

1949 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1950 f"{cls.__name__}.{name}{origin} must be 'async def' on an " 

1951 f"async view, which awaits it. Write 'async def {name}', and " 

1952 f"'await super().{name}(...)'." 

1953 ) 

1954 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

1955 f"{cls.__name__}.{name}{origin} is 'async def', but a sync view " 

1956 f"calls it without await. Write 'def {name}', or use " 

1957 "fr.AsyncRestView." 

1958 )

1961def _origin(cls: type, klass: type) -> str: 

1962 """`` (from AppView)`` when ``klass`` is a base class of ``cls``.""" 

1963 return "" if klass is cls else f" (from {klass.__name__})" 

1964 

1965 

1966def _owner(cls: type, name: str) -> type: 

1967 """The class in the MRO of ``cls`` that sets ``name``, or ``cls`` when 

1968 none does.""" 

1969 return next((klass for klass in cls.__mro__ if name in vars(klass)), cls) 

1970 

1971 

1972def _set_by(cls: type, name: str) -> str: 

1973 """`` (from AppView)`` when a base class of ``cls`` sets ``name``.""" 

1974 return _origin(cls, _owner(cls, name)) 

1975 

1976 

1977def _how_set(cls: type, name: str) -> str: 

1978 """How ``cls`` has the list setting ``name``, for a message, such as 

1979 ``inherits include_filters = ('*', '*.*') from AppView``.""" 

1980 value = _list_setting(cls, name) 

1981 setter = _owner(cls, name) 

1982 if value == _LIST_SETTING_DEFAULTS[name]: 

1983 return f"has {name} = {value!r}" 

1984 if setter is cls: 

1985 return f"sets {name} = {value!r}" 

1986 return f"inherits {name} = {value!r} from {setter.__name__}" 

1987

2045def _route_parameters(route: Callable[..., Any]) -> Mapping[str, inspect.Parameter]: 

2046 """The parameters of ``route``, without evaluating its annotations. 

2047 

2048 On 3.14 a route may name a class that its module defines further down, 

2049 because annotations are read only when asked for. Evaluating them while 

2050 the view class is defined would raise ``NameError`` for that name. 

2051 """ 

2052 if sys.version_info >= (3, 14): 2052 ↛ 2053line 2052 didn't jump to line 2053 because the condition on line 2052 was never true

2053 return inspect.signature( 

2054 route, annotation_format=annotationlib.Format.FORWARDREF 

2055 ).parameters 

2056 return inspect.signature(route).parameters

2059def _check_removed_settings(cls: type) -> None: 

2060 """Reject a setting that Restly no longer reads. Without this a guard in 

2061 ``route_options`` would stop running, and nothing would say so.""" 

2062 for klass in cls.__mro__: 

2063 for name, instead in _REMOVED_SETTINGS.items(): 

2064 if name in vars(klass): 

2065 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

2066 f"{cls.__name__} sets {name}{_origin(cls, klass)}, which was " 

2067 f"removed. {instead}" 

2068 ) 

2069 

2070 

2071def _check_renamed_names(cls: type) -> None: 

2072 """Reject a setting, a method or a route parameter that still uses a name 

2073 from before the rename. Runs when the class is defined and again at 

2074 registration, so a value assigned to the class later is caught too.""" 

2075 _check_removed_settings(cls) 

2076 for klass in cls.__mro__: 

2077 origin = _origin(cls, klass) 

2078 for old, new in _RENAMED_SETTINGS.items(): 

2079 if old in vars(klass): 

2080 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

2081 f"{cls.__name__} sets {old}{origin}, which was renamed to " 

2082 f"{new}. Rename the setting." 

2083 ) 

2084 for old, new in _RENAMED_METHODS.items(): 

2085 if old in vars(klass): 

2086 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

2087 f"{cls.__name__} defines {old}{origin}, which was renamed " 

2088 f"to {new}.{_RENAMED_METHOD_HINTS.get(old, '')} Rename the " 

2089 "method." 

2090 ) 

2091 for name, value in vars(klass).items(): 

2092 if not hasattr(value, "_api_route_args"): 

2093 continue 

2094 if "query_params" in _route_parameters(value): 

2095 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

2096 f"{cls.__name__}.{name}{origin} declares a query_params " 

2097 "parameter, which was renamed to list_params. Rename the " 

2098 "parameter, so the route still takes the filter, sort and " 

2099 "page parameters." 

2100 )

2102 

2103class BaseRestView( 

2104 View, Generic[ModelT, ResponseSchemaT, CreateSchemaT, UpdateSchemaT, IdT] 

2105): 

2106 """ 

2107 The part that :class:`RestView` and :class:`AsyncRestView` share: the 

2108 settings, the read statement and the response methods. 

2109 

2110 It has no routes, no handlers and no business methods. Those are on 

2111 ``RestView`` and ``AsyncRestView``, in a sync and an async form. Subclass 

2112 this class only to write a CRUD base class of your own. 

2113 """ 

2114 

2115 responses: ClassVar[dict[int | str, dict[str, Any]]] = { 

2116 404: {"description": "Not found"} 

2117 } 

2118 

2119 # The view's actions: the names that authorize and the transaction hooks 

2120 # get. A view with actions of its own declares a subclass of fr.Action 

2121 # with this name. (The docs show fr.Action, not this attribute.) 

2122 Action = Action 

2123 

2124 #: The view's schema: the Pydantic class that lists the fields of the 

2125 #: resource. Restly builds :attr:`schema_response`, :attr:`schema_create` 

2126 #: and :attr:`schema_update` from it. When a view sets none, Restly 

2127 #: generates it from :attr:`model` with 

2128 #: :func:`~fastapi_restly.schemas.derive_schema`. 

2129 schema: ClassVar[type[pydantic.BaseModel]] 

2130 #: The class of everything that goes out: the single responses, the 

2131 #: items of the list response, and the fields the list params filter and 

2132 #: sort on. The relationships it names are the ones the view loads. When 

2133 #: a view sets none, Restly builds it with 

2134 #: :func:`~fastapi_restly.schemas.derive_schema_response`: the view's 

2135 #: schema without its ``WriteOnly`` fields, named ``<Resource>Response``. 

2136 #: A class that a view sets is used as it is. 

2137 schema_response: ClassVar[type[pydantic.BaseModel]] 

2138 #: The class of the ``POST`` body. When a view sets none, Restly builds 

2139 #: it from the view's schema without its ``ReadOnly`` fields and without 

2140 #: a primary key that the server generates. It is named 

2141 #: ``<Resource>Create``. A class that a view sets is used as it is. 

2142 schema_create: ClassVar[type[pydantic.BaseModel]] 

2143 #: The class of the ``PATCH`` body. When a view sets none, Restly builds 

2144 #: it from the view's schema without its ``ReadOnly`` fields and without 

2145 #: a primary key that the server generates, and makes every other field 

2146 #: optional. It is named ``<Resource>Update``. A class that a view sets 

2147 #: is used as it is. 

2148 schema_update: ClassVar[type[pydantic.BaseModel]] 

2149 #: The SQLAlchemy model that the view serves: a mapped class. A view that 

2150 #: you register needs it. A class that is not mapped raises 

2151 #: :class:`~fastapi_restly.exc.RestlyConfigurationError` when Python 

2152 #: creates the view class. 

2153 model: ClassVar[type[Any]] 

2154 #: The clause every read on this view applies: list, count, and retrieve 

2155 #: (a row outside it is 404). ``None`` (the default) falls back to the 

2156 #: model's declared ``default_scope``; ``fr.clauses.UNSCOPED`` reads 

2157 #: unscoped despite that default. Declaring a scope replaces the default, 

2158 #: it does not stack on it; compose the replacement from the same leaves 

2159 #: (``ItemClauses.trashed`` containing the tenant clause ``visible`` 

2160 #: contains). A rule that must hold under every scope is a session-level 

2161 #: ``with_loader_criteria``, not a view concern (see the Multi-Tenancy 

2162 #: guide). See the Scopes guide for scopes. 

2163 scope: ClassVar[WhereClause | None] = None 

2164 #: The type of the ``{id}`` path parameter on the default routes. ``None`` 

2165 #: (the default) takes the Python type of the model's primary key, and a 

2166 #: composite key gets ``int``. Set a type to override it. Built-in item 

2167 #: routes use Starlette's ``int`` or ``uuid`` path converter for those 

2168 #: types. Integer paths accept non-negative digits. An unmatched value 

2169 #: falls through to another route or returns 404, instead of 422. 

2170 id_type: ClassVar[type[Any] | None] = None 

2171 #: The routes that the view serves, such as 

2172 #: ``(fr.ViewRoute.GET_MANY, fr.ViewRoute.GET_ONE)``: :class:`ViewRoute` 

2173 #: values for the CRUD routes, or the names of route methods, also of a 

2174 #: custom route. The view leaves out every other route, also a route that 

2175 #: a base view gets later. The default, ``("*",)``, is every route. A 

2176 #: subclass that sets its own value replaces the list of its base. A name 

2177 #: that is not a route raises ``AttributeError`` when the view is 

2178 #: registered. 

2179 include_routes: ClassVar[Collection[str | ViewRoute]] = ("*",) 

2180 #: The routes to leave out of the view, after :attr:`include_routes`, 

2181 #: such as ``(fr.ViewRoute.DELETE,)``: :class:`ViewRoute` values for the 

2182 #: CRUD routes, or the names of endpoint methods. A subclass that sets its

2368 def _apply_scope(self, stmt: Select[Any], scope: ReadScope) -> Select[Any]: 

2369 # the one path every read takes, so retrieve, list and count cannot 

2370 # disagree about which rows exist; not an override point 

2371 if scope is None: 

2372 scope = resolve_scope(self) 

2373 else: 

2374 # a per-read scope replaces the resolution rather than joining it 

2375 scope = _checked_scope(scope, type(self).__name__, "a per-read scope") 

2376 return apply_clauses(stmt, scope) 

2377 

2378 def _narrowed_scope(self, scope: ReadScope, where: _ReadWhere) -> ReadScope: 

2379 # the list handler is final, so it can fold where= into the scope it 

2380 # forwards: get_many keeps one visibility input, and an override 

2381 # keeps its signature 

2382 if where is None: 

2383 return scope 

2384 label = type(self).__name__ 

2385 if scope is None: 

2386 scope = resolve_scope(self) 

2387 else: 

2388 scope = _checked_scope(scope, label, "a per-read scope") 

2389 return all_of(scope, _checked_where(where, label))

2391 @final 

2392 def select(self, *, scope: ReadScope = None) -> Select[Any]: 

2393 """The statement of the view's rows: ``select(model)``, the scope, 

2394 and :meth:`get_loader_options`. 

2395 

2396 ``get_one`` and ``get_many`` start here, and so does a custom route 

2397 that builds its own read: ``self.select().where(Item.price > 10)``. 

2398 The rows are the ones the view shows, and each row loads what the 

2399 response needs. Final: set ``scope`` to change the rows, and override 

2400 :meth:`get_loader_options` to change the loads. 

2401 

2402 :param scope: a clause that replaces the view scope for this 

2403 statement; ``fr.clauses.UNSCOPED`` reads past it. 

2404 """ 

2405 stmt = self._apply_scope(sa_select(self.model), scope) 

2406 options = self.get_loader_options() 

2407 return stmt.options(*options) if options else stmt

2461 """The loader options of every read: what each row loads.

2468 a ``query_expression`` through ``with_expression(...)``. Add to 

2469 ``super().get_loader_options()`` to keep the default loads. See

2477 def _get_reload_statements(self, subject: Any, others: list[Any]) -> list[Any]: 

2478 """The SELECTs that make the saved rows of a write ready for the 

2479 hooks and the response. 

2480 

2481 Called by the save step of the commit bracket after the flush and the 

2482 refresh of the subject. One reload covers the subject, when the view 

2483 has loader options, and the other rows of the view's model that the 

2484 action wrote. So a value that only the loader options load, such as 

2485 a relationship that ``to_single_response`` reads or a 

2486 ``with_expression``, is there after every write, and a route that 

2487 changes several rows returns each of them as the database has it. 

2488 The view's scope does not apply: a row that the write moved out of 

2489 it, such as a soft-deleted row, is still the row that the action 

2490 returns. 

2491 """ 

2492 rows = list(others) 

2493 options = self.get_loader_options() 

2494 if options and isinstance(subject, self.model): 

2495 if sa_inspect(subject).persistent: 

2496 rows.insert(0, subject) 

2497 if not rows: 

2498 return [] 

2499 return _rows_reload_statements(self.model, rows, options)

3190#: A ``BaseRestView`` at any parameterization, for the signature below. 

3191_AnyRestView = BaseRestView[Any, Any, Any, Any, Any]

3194def resolve_scope(target: type[Any] | _AnyRestView) -> WhereClause: 

3195 """The scope a read applies, resolved down the ladder. 

3196 

3197 Pass a view, class or instance, for the visibility that view's reads 

3198 apply: its declared 

3199 :attr:`scope <fastapi_restly.views.BaseRestView.scope>`, the model's 

3200 ``default_scope`` when the view declares none, and 

3201 ``fr.clauses.UNSCOPED`` when neither does. Pass a mapped model class 

3202 for the model rung alone, which is what every reference check applies. 

3203 The two answers differ wherever a view declares a scope, so code off 

3204 the request path that wants what the API shows passes the view. 

3205 

3206 The result is a clause or ``fr.clauses.UNSCOPED``, never ``None``, so 

3207 it composes without a branch:: 

3208 

3209 stmt = fr.apply_clauses( 

3210 select(Task).where(Task.project_id == id), 

3211 fr.resolve_scope(TaskView), 

3212 ) 

3213 

3214 Every read resolves here, so a route that applies the result sees the 

3215 same rows as 

3216 :meth:`get_one <fastapi_restly.views.RestView.get_one>` and 

3217 :meth:`get_many <fastapi_restly.views.RestView.get_many>`. It resolves 

3218 the scope and does not apply it: applying stays with the framework, 

3219 and there is no apply-side override point. 

3220 

3221 :param target: a view class or instance, or a mapped model class. 

3222 :raises RestlyConfigurationError: if the declared scope is not a clause. 

3223 :raises TypeError: if ``target`` is neither a view nor a mapped model. 

3224 """ 

3225 label = target.__name__ if isinstance(target, type) else type(target).__name__ 

3226 if is_mapped_class(target): 

3227 return _model_scope(target) 

3228 if not isinstance(target, BaseRestView) and not ( 

3229 isinstance(target, type) and issubclass(target, BaseRestView) 

3230 ): 

3231 raise TypeError( 

3232 "resolve_scope() takes a RestView / AsyncRestView class or instance, " 

3233 f"or a mapped model class, got {label}" 

3234 ) 

3235 declared = target.scope 

3236 if declared is None: 

3237 return _model_scope(target.model) 

3238 # backstop for a post-definition assignment; the declared form is 

3239 # validated in __init_subclass__ 

3240 return _checked_scope(declared, label, "the scope") 

3241 

3242 

3243def _model_scope(model: type[Any]) -> WhereClause: 

3244 declared = _default_scope(model) 

3245 return UNSCOPED if declared is None else declared 

3246

3248def _checked_scope(scope: Any, label: str, what: str) -> WhereClause: 

3249 if isinstance(scope, WhereClause): 

3250 return scope 

3251 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

3252 f"{label}: {what} must be a WhereClause or fr.clauses.UNSCOPED, got " 

3253 f"{type(scope).__name__}; wrap a raw expression with where_clause()"

3257def _clause_element(value: Any) -> Any: 

3258 """The SQL expression behind a mapped column or a hybrid property, such 

3259 as ``Item.archived``, which ``.where()`` accepts too. Other values are 

3260 returned as they are.""" 

3261 if isinstance(value, QueryableAttribute): 

3262 return value.__clause_element__() 

3263 return value

3266def _checked_where(where: Any, label: str) -> WhereClause: 

3267 if isinstance(where, WhereClause): 

3268 return where 

3269 where = _clause_element(where) 

3270 if isinstance(where, ColumnElement): 

3271 return where_clause(where) 

3272 if type(where) is bool: 

3273 # ``obj.slug == slug`` on a loaded object is a Python bool, and 

3274 # SQLAlchemy renders it as WHERE true, which narrows nothing 

3275 raise TypeError( 

3276 f"{label}: where= got a bool, not a SQL expression. A comparison " 

3277 "on an instance attribute is a bool; compare the column instead " 

3278 "(Model.slug == slug)." 

3279 ) 

3280 raise TypeError( 

3281 f"{label}: where= must be a SQLAlchemy boolean expression or a clause, " 

3282 f"got {type(where).__name__}"

3286def _check_identity_tables( 

3287 model_cls: type[Any], id: ColumnElement[bool], label: str 

3288) -> None: 

3289 """Raise when the expression that picks the row names another table. 

3290 

3291 SQLAlchemy adds such a table to the FROM of the query, which joins every 

3292 row of it, so ``Shelf.id == 2`` in a view of books picks a book that has 

3293 nothing to do with shelf 2. 

3294 """ 

3295 missing = _expression_tables(id) - _statement_tables(sa_select(model_cls)) 

3296 if missing: 

3297 name = model_cls.__name__ 

3298 shown = ", ".join(sorted(_display_table_name(key) for key in missing)) 

3299 raise TypeError( 

3300 f"{label}: the expression that picks the row names a table that is " 

3301 f"not in the query: {shown}. It would join every row of that " 

3302 f"table, so a wrong row could be loaded. Compare a column of " 

3303 f"{name}, such as {name}.slug == slug, or use .has() or .any() " 

3304 "for a related row." 

3305 ) 

3306 

3307 

3308def _reject_bad_row_identity(label: str, id: Any) -> None:

3310 if isinstance(id, WhereClause): 

3311 raise TypeError( 

3312 f"{label}: a clause is a scope, not a row identity. " 

3313 "Call it for its expression (ItemClauses.published()), or " 

3314 "pass it as scope= to replace the view scope for this read." 

3315 ) 

3316 if type(id) is bool: 

3317 # ``obj.slug == slug`` on a loaded object is a Python bool, and 

3318 # SQLAlchemy renders it as WHERE true, which matches the whole scope 

3319 raise TypeError( 

3320 f"{label}: got a bool, not an id or a SQL expression. " 

3321 "A comparison on an instance attribute is a bool; compare the " 

3322 "column instead (Model.slug == slug)." 

3323 )

3326def _primary_key_criterion(model_cls: type[Any], id: Any) -> ColumnElement[bool]: 

3327 """The default :meth:`BaseRestView.where_id`: the primary key is ``id``. 

3328 

3329 :raises RequestValidationError: ``id`` does not fit the key column, such 

3330 as a number out of the range of an ``Integer``. The database would 

3331 refuse it with an error. 

3332 """ 

3333 pk_cols = sa_inspect(model_cls).primary_key 

3334 if len(pk_cols) != 1: 

3335 raise NotImplementedError( 

3336 f"{model_cls.__name__} has a composite primary key, so an id does " 

3337 "not name one row. Override where_id(id): split the id from the " 

3338 "path, and return sqlalchemy.and_(Model.a == a, Model.b == b)." 

3339 ) 

3340 try: 

3341 id = column_value(pk_cols[0].type, id) 

3342 except ValueError as exc: 

3343 raise RequestValidationError( 

3344 [ 

3345 { 

3346 "type": "value_error", 

3347 "loc": ("path", "id"), 

3348 "msg": value_error_reason(exc), 

3349 "input": id, 

3350 "ctx": {"error": exc}, 

3351 } 

3352 ] 

3353 ) from None 

3354 return pk_cols[0] == id

3365def reject_unknown_query_keys( 

3366 query: QueryParams, allowed: set[str], request: fastapi.Request | None 

3367) -> None: 

3368 """Raise a 422 naming every key of ``query`` that is not in ``allowed``. 

3369 

3370 The list params decide what is allowed: their keys for the default list 

3371 params, ``sort``/``range``/``filter`` for react-admin. A key that the 

3372 route of ``request`` reads elsewhere is never unknown (see 

3373 :func:`_route_query_keys`). 

3374 

3375 :raises RequestValidationError: ``query`` has an unknown key. 

3376 """ 

3377 unknown = set(query.keys()) - allowed 

3378 if unknown and request is not None: 

3379 unknown -= _route_query_keys(request) 

3380 if unknown: 

3381 raise _unknown_keys_error(query, unknown)

3384def _unknown_keys_error(query: QueryParams, keys: set[str]) -> RequestValidationError: 

3385 """The error for unknown query keys, in the shape of FastAPI's own 

3386 validation errors.""" 

3387 return RequestValidationError( 

3388 [ 

3389 { 

3390 "type": "extra_forbidden", 

3391 "loc": ("query", key), 

3392 "msg": f"Unknown query parameter {key!r}", 

3393 "input": query.get(key), 

3394 } 

3395 for key in sorted(keys) 

3396 ] 

3397 )

3400def _route_query_keys(request: fastapi.Request) -> set[str]: 

3401 """The query keys that the matched route reads. 

3402 

3403 Every query parameter its dependency tree declares, at any level: the 

3404 app or a router, the view's ``dependencies``, a class attribute, the 

3405 endpoint. Also the key of a query API key scheme such as 

3406 ``APIKeyQuery``, which reads the query string without declaring a 

3407 parameter. The guard walks the tree only for a key that the list 

3408 params do not have. 

3409 """ 

3410 dependant = getattr(matched_route(request.scope), "dependant", None) 

3411 pending = [dependant] if dependant is not None else [] 

3412 keys: set[str] = set() 

3413 while pending: 

3414 current = pending.pop() 

3415 for field in current.query_params: 

3416 # the name FastAPI reads the value from 

3417 keys.add(getattr(field, "validation_alias", None) or field.alias) 

3418 call = current.call 

3419 if isinstance(call, APIKeyBase) and call.model.in_ == APIKeyIn.query: 

3420 keys.add(call.model.name) 

3421 pending.extend(current.dependencies) 

3422 return keys

3425def _list_params_dependency( 

3426 params_model: type[pydantic.BaseModel], 

3427) -> Callable[..., pydantic.BaseModel]: 

3428 """A dependency that validates ``params_model`` from the query string. 

3429 

3430 FastAPI splits a query model into its fields only when it is the sole 

3431 query parameter: at runtime per function, in OpenAPI across the route. 

3432 Any other query parameter therefore collapses it into one required 

3433 ``list_params`` value. This reads the fields itself, the way FastAPI 

3434 hands a query model its input: every value of a repeated key for a 

3435 sequence field, the last value otherwise, a default that is not None, 

3436 and any other key as sent. :func:`_list_openapi_parameters` 

3437 documents the fields. 

3438 """ 

3439 fields = _list_params_fields(params_model) 

3440 

3441 def list_params(request: fastapi.Request, first: Any = None) -> pydantic.BaseModel: 

3442 return _validate_list_params(params_model, fields, request.query_params) 

3443 

3444 parameters = [ 

3445 inspect.Parameter( 

3446 "request", inspect.Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY, annotation=fastapi.Request 

3447 ) 

3448 ] 

3449 if fields: 

3450 # FastAPI documents a route's 422 only when it reads a parameter of 

3451 # the route itself. It reads the first key here, undocumented and 

3452 # unchecked; the model validates the value with the rest. 

3453 marker = fastapi.Query(alias=fields[0][0], include_in_schema=False) 

3454 parameters.append( 

3455 inspect.Parameter( 

3456 "first", 

3457 inspect.Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY, 

3458 default=None, 

3459 annotation=Annotated[Any, marker], 

3460 ) 

3461 ) 

3462 list_params.__signature__ = inspect.Signature(parameters) # type: ignore[attr-defined] 

3463 return list_params

3465 

3466#: The query key of each field of a list params model, the field, and 

3467#: whether the field reads every value of a repeated key. 

3468_ListParamsFields = tuple[tuple[str, FieldInfo, bool], ...] 

3469 

3470_LIST_PARAMS_FIELDS: "weakref.WeakKeyDictionary[type, _ListParamsFields]" = ( 

3471 weakref.WeakKeyDictionary() 

3472)

3475def _list_params_fields(params_model: type[pydantic.BaseModel]) -> _ListParamsFields: 

3476 # once per model: a raw QueryParams or mapping reads them on every call 

3477 fields = _LIST_PARAMS_FIELDS.get(params_model) 

3478 if fields is None: 

3479 fields = tuple( 

3480 (_query_key(name, field), field, _reads_every_value(field)) 

3481 for name, field in params_model.model_fields.items() 

3482 ) 

3483 _LIST_PARAMS_FIELDS[params_model] = fields 

3484 return fields

3487def _validate_list_params(

3489 fields: _ListParamsFields, 

3490 query: QueryParams, 

3491) -> pydantic.BaseModel:

3493 query model.

3495 :raises RequestValidationError: a value fails the validation of its 

3496 field. The location of each error starts with ``"query"``. 

3497 """ 

3498 field_keys = {key for key, _, _ in fields} 

3499 data: dict[str, Any] = {} 

3500 for key, field, every_value in fields: 

3501 if key in query: 

3502 data[key] = query.getlist(key) if every_value else query[key] 

3503 elif not field.is_required(): 3503 ↛ 3500line 3503 didn't jump to line 3500 because the condition on line 3503 was always true

3504 default = field.get_default() 

3505 if default is not None: 

3506 data[key] = default 

3507 for key in query.keys(): 

3508 if key not in field_keys: 

3509 values = query.getlist(key) 

3510 data[key] = values[0] if len(values) == 1 else values 

3511 try: 

3512 return params_model.model_validate(data) 

3513 except pydantic.ValidationError as exc: 

3514 errors = [ 

3515 {**error, "loc": ("query", *error["loc"])}

3521def _validate_raw_list_params( 

3522 params_model: type[pydantic.BaseModel], raw: Any 

3523) -> pydantic.BaseModel:

3568def _is_sequence_annotation(annotation: Any) -> bool:

3572 isinstance(candidate, type)

3580def _list_openapi_parameters( 

3581 params_model: type[pydantic.BaseModel], 

3582) -> list[dict[str, Any]]: 

3583 """One OpenAPI query parameter per field of ``params_model``. 

3584 

3585 The entries FastAPI writes for a query model it splits into fields, so 

3586 the list route documents the same whatever else the route reads. Built from 

3587 the model's JSON schema, with references inlined: the document's 

3588 components do not hold the model's definitions.

3590 schema = params_model.model_json_schema() 

3591 definitions = schema.get("$defs", {}) 

3592 properties = schema.get("properties", {}) 

3593 required = set(schema.get("required", ())) 

3594 parameters: list[dict[str, Any]] = [] 

3595 for name, field in params_model.model_fields.items(): 

3596 key = _query_key(name, field) 

3597 field_schema = _inline_definitions( 

3598 properties.get(key, properties.get(name, {})), definitions 

3599 ) 

3600 field_schema["title"] = field.title or key.title().replace("_", " ") 

3601 parameter: dict[str, Any] = { 

3602 "name": key, 

3603 "in": "query", 

3604 "required": key in required, 

3605 "schema": field_schema, 

3606 } 

3607 if field.description: 

3608 parameter["description"] = field.description 

3609 if field.deprecated: 3609 ↛ 3610line 3609 didn't jump to line 3610 because the condition on line 3609 was never true

3610 parameter["deprecated"] = True 

3611 parameters.append(parameter) 

3612 return parameters

3615def _inline_definitions(schema: Any, definitions: dict[str, Any]) -> Any: 

3616 """``schema`` with each ``#/$defs/...`` reference replaced by its target.""" 

3617 if isinstance(schema, list): 

3618 return [_inline_definitions(item, definitions) for item in schema] 

3619 if not isinstance(schema, dict): 

3620 return schema 

3621 inlined = { 

3622 key: _inline_definitions(value, definitions) 

3623 for key, value in schema.items() 

3624 if key != "$ref" 

3625 } 

3626 reference = schema.get("$ref") 

3627 if isinstance(reference, str) and reference.startswith("#/$defs/"): 3627 ↛ 3628line 3627 didn't jump to line 3628 because the condition on line 3627 was never true

3628 target = definitions[reference.removeprefix("#/$defs/")] 

3629 return {**_inline_definitions(target, definitions), **inlined} 

3630 return inlined

3633def _guard_list_params(route: Callable) -> Callable: 

3634 """Run the unknown-key guard before a route that takes ``list_params``. 

3635 

3636 A copy, like the parent-endpoint copies: it keeps the route args and the 

3637 signature. The marker keeps a subclass's copy from being wrapped twice. 

3638 """ 

3639 if inspect.iscoroutinefunction(route): 

3640 

3641 async def _async_guarded(self, *args, **kwargs): 

3642 self._reject_unknown_query_params() 

3643 return await route(self, *args, **kwargs) 

3644 

3645 guarded: Callable = _async_guarded 

3646 else: 

3647 

3648 def _sync_guarded(self, *args, **kwargs): 

3649 self._reject_unknown_query_params() 

3650 return route(self, *args, **kwargs) 

3651 

3652 guarded = _sync_guarded 

3653 

3654 guarded = _wrap_endpoint(guarded, route) 

3655 guarded._fr_list_guard = True # type: ignore[attr-defined] 

3656 return guarded

3659def _route_names(view_cls: type, setting: str) -> frozenset[str]: 

3660 """The endpoint method names that the view's ``include_routes`` or 

3661 ``exclude_routes`` names. 

3662 

3663 :raises RestlyConfigurationError: the setting is one string, such as 

3664 ``(fr.ViewRoute.GET_MANY)`` without the comma of a tuple. A string is 

3665 a collection of its characters, so it would name the routes ``"g"``, 

3666 ``"e"`` and so on. 

3667 """ 

3668 value = getattr(view_cls, setting) 

3669 if isinstance(value, str): 

3670 if isinstance(value, ViewRoute): 

3671 shown = got = f"fr.ViewRoute.{value.name}" 

3672 else: 

3673 shown, got = repr(value), f"the string {value!r}" 

3674 raise RestlyConfigurationError( 

3675 f"{view_cls.__name__}.{setting}{_set_by(view_cls, setting)} must be " 

3676 f"a tuple of routes, got {got}. For one entry, write " 

3677 f"{setting} = ({shown},) with a comma." 

3678 ) 

3679 return frozenset( 

3680 route.value if isinstance(route, ViewRoute) else route for route in value 

3681 )

3684def _serves_route(view_cls: type, method_name: str) -> bool: 

3685 """True if the CRUD view serves the route method ``method_name``: it has a 

3686 route method of that name, its ``include_routes`` has it, and its 

3687 ``exclude_routes`` does not.""" 

3688 if not hasattr(getattr(view_cls, method_name, None), "_api_route_args"): 

3689 return False 

3690 included = _route_names(view_cls, "include_routes") 

3691 return ("*" in included or method_name in included) and ( 

3692 method_name not in _route_names(view_cls, "exclude_routes") 

3693 )

3695 

3696def _check_route_settings(cls: type[BaseRestView[Any, Any, Any, Any, Any]]): 

3697 """Raise for a name in ``include_routes`` or ``exclude_routes`` that is no 

3698 route at all: a typo, or the business method name instead of the 

3699 ``*_endpoint`` route name. ``"*"`` in ``include_routes`` is every route. 

3700 

3701 The routes that the view leaves out stay routes on the class. The router 

3702 leaves them out. So a subclass with its own settings gets them back, also 

3703 when the base registered first and copied them into its own namespace. 

3704 """ 

3705 for setting in ("include_routes", "exclude_routes"): 

3706 for method_name in sorted(_route_names(cls, setting)): 

3707 if setting == "include_routes" and method_name == "*": 

3708 continue 

3709 if not _is_route_name_in_lineage(cls, method_name): 

3710 raise AttributeError( 

3711 f"{method_name!r} in {setting} is not a route on {cls.__name__}" 

3712 )

3714 

3715def _is_route_name_in_lineage( 

3716 cls: type[BaseRestView[Any, Any, Any, Any, Any]], method_name: str 

3717) -> bool: 

3718 """True if any class in ``cls``'s MRO defines a routable endpoint of this 

3719 name.""" 

3720 return any( 

3721 hasattr(klass.__dict__.get(method_name), "_api_route_args") 

3722 for klass in cls.mro() 

3723 )

3726def _init_view_cls_and_add_to_router( 

3727 view_cls: type[View], parent_router: fastapi.APIRouter | fastapi.FastAPI 

3728): 

3729 """ 

3730 FastAPI builds routes from callable signatures and annotations. View classes 

3731 need a small adapter layer before registration; that preparation happens here. 

3732 

3733 FastAPI does a lot with annotations. For example, accepted or returned JSON is 

3734 often described with Pydantic classes like this: 

3735 

3736 def my_endpoint(foo: FooSchema) -> FooSchema: 

3737 

3738 Most of this preparation sets the correct annotations on inherited class 

3739 methods. 

3740 

3741 The class-level preparation (copying parent endpoints, renaming, annotating, 

3742 schema generation, dataclass-style __init__) only runs once per View class — 

3743 subsequent calls to ``include_view()`` reuse the prepared class and only 

3744 construct a fresh APIRouter to mount on the new parent. This makes 

3745 registering the same view on *different* routers safe (e.g. a public app and 

3746 an admin app, or ``/v1`` and ``/v2`` sub-apps). 

3747 

3748 Re-registering the same view on the *same* parent is a no-op (flagged by 

3749 the opt-in misuse lint): each parent tracks the view classes already 

3750 mounted on it, so a duplicate ``include_view()`` call (double import, 

3751 decorator plus explicit call) cannot mount the same routes twice. 

3752 """ 

3753 # A FastAPI app delegates include_router to its .router; track mounted 

3754 # views on the router so app and app.router count as one parent. 

3755 holder = ( 

3756 parent_router.router 

3757 if isinstance(parent_router, fastapi.FastAPI) 

3758 else parent_router 

3759 ) 

3760 mounted: set[type[View]] = getattr(holder, "_fr_mounted_views", None) or set() 

3761 if view_cls in mounted: 

3762 if _fr_config.warn_on_misuse: 

3763 warnings.warn( 

3764 f"{view_cls.__name__} is already registered on this app/router; " 

3765 f"this include_view() call is a no-op. Duplicate registration " 

3766 f"usually means a double import or the decorator form combined " 

3767 f"with an explicit include_view() call.", 

3768 RestlyMisuseWarning, 

3769 stacklevel=4, 

3770 ) 

3771 return 

3772 _prepare_view_class(view_cls) 

3773 api_router = _init_api_router(view_cls) 

3774 _register_for_resource_ref(parent_router, view_cls) 

3775 parent_router.include_router(api_router) 

3776 # Record only after the mount succeeded: a failed registration must not be 

3777 # marked as mounted, or the next call would silently no-op a view whose 

3778 # routes never made it onto the parent. 

3779 mounted.add(view_cls) 

3780 setattr(holder, "_fr_mounted_views", mounted) 

3781 

3782 

3783#: The five endpoint methods defined by RestView / AsyncRestView. 

3784_ENDPOINT_METHOD_NAMES = frozenset( 

3785 { 

3786 "get_many_endpoint", 

3787 "get_one_endpoint", 

3788 "create_endpoint", 

3789 "update_endpoint", 

3790 "delete_endpoint", 

3791 } 

3792)

3797 has none, such as for a function that was built at run time.""" 

3798 func = getattr(value, "__func__", value) 

3799 if not isinstance(func, types.FunctionType): 

3800 return ""

3802 return inspect.getsource(func)

3807def _warn_on_misuse(view_cls: type[View]) -> None: 

3808 """Opt-in registration-time lint (``fr.configure(warn_on_misuse=True)``). 

3809 

3810 Flags the dominant misuse patterns with the idiomatic fix named in 

3811 each message. Heuristic, best-effort, and advisory: every pattern it flags 

3812 has a legitimate use, so it warns (:class:`RestlyMisuseWarning`) rather 

3813 than rejects. Must run *before* parent endpoints are copied into the 

3814 subclass, while ``__dict__`` still holds only what the user wrote; only 

3815 the registered class is linted, not user-defined intermediate bases. 

3816 """ 

3817 own = view_cls.__dict__ 

3818 name = view_cls.__name__ 

3819 

3820 # 1. Endpoint-method override where a business-method override was likely 

3821 # meant. A replacement that calls the handler, or the endpoint method of 

3822 # its base, keeps the steps: that is how a view changes the HTTP contract. 

3823 if issubclass(view_cls, BaseRestView): 

3824 for endpoint in sorted(_ENDPOINT_METHOD_NAMES & own.keys()): 

3825 verb = endpoint.removesuffix("_endpoint") 

3826 source = _source_of(own[endpoint]) 

3827 if f"handle_{verb}(" in source or f"super().{endpoint}(" in source: 

3828 continue 

3829 if verb in _WRITE_VERBS: 3829 ↛ 3830line 3829 didn't jump to line 3830 because the condition on line 3829 was never true

3830 seams = f"For domain logic override the business method '{verb}'" 

3831 keep = "the bracket" 

3832 else: 

3833 lookup = "where_id" if verb == "get_one" else "apply_list_params" 

3834 seams = f"For the rows override 'scope', for the lookup '{lookup}'" 

3835 keep = "the gate" 

3836 warnings.warn( 

3837 f"{name} overrides the endpoint method '{endpoint}'. Override " 

3838 f"an endpoint method only to change the HTTP contract. {seams}; " 

3839 f"for a gate 'authorize'; for the response shape 'to_response'. " 

3840 f"Call 'handle_{verb}' from the replacement to keep {keep}.", 

3841 RestlyMisuseWarning, 

3842 stacklevel=5, 

3843 ) 

3844 

3845 # 2. Manual session.commit() in a view method. The framework owns the 

3846 # commit; methods that go through write_action / handle_<verb> are exempt. 

3847 for attr, value in own.items(): 

3848 source = _source_of(value) 

3849 if ( 

3850 ".commit(" in source 

3851 and "write_action" not in source 

3852 and "handle_" not in source 

3853 ): 

3854 warnings.warn( 

3855 f"{name}.{attr} calls session.commit() directly. The framework " 

3856 f"owns the commit: reuse handle_<verb>(), or bracket the " 

3857 f"mutation with write_action(self.Action.<NAME>, ...) so authorize / " 

3858 f"before_action_commit / after_action_commit run.", 

3859 RestlyMisuseWarning, 

3860 stacklevel=5, 

3861 ) 

3862 

3863 # 3. A reference type (IDRef/IDSchema) whose name is a scalar FK column: 

3864 # the ``post_id: IDRef[Post]`` mistake, where ``data.post_id`` becomes a 

3865 # wrapper instead of the plain id. 

3866 _warn_scalar_named_reference_fields(view_cls) 

3867 

3868 # 4. A writable field on a column that the model sets, such as a tenant 

3869 # or an audit column: the request body replaces the column default. 

3870 _warn_writable_model_set_fields(view_cls) 

3871

3873def _warn_scalar_named_reference_fields(view_cls: type[View]) -> None: 

3874 """Flag an ``IDRef``/``IDSchema`` field whose name is a scalar foreign-key 

3875 column: ``post_id: IDRef[Post]`` makes ``data.post_id`` a reference wrapper 

3876 instead of the plain id. Steer to ``fr.MustExist[pk, Model]``. Best-effort: 

3877 lints only an explicitly-declared ``schema`` against the view's ``model``, 

3878 and never a relationship-named or list reference (those names aren't columns). 

3879 """ 

3880 schema = view_cls.__dict__.get("schema") 

3881 model = getattr(view_cls, "model", None) 

3882 if schema is None or model is None: 

3883 return 

3884 try: 

3885 mapper = sa_inspect(model) 

3886 except Exception: 

3887 return 

3888 for field_name, field_info in schema.model_fields.items(): 

3889 origin_target = reference_origin_and_target(field_info.annotation) 

3890 if origin_target is None: 

3891 continue 

3892 column = mapper.columns.get(field_name) 

3893 if column is None or not column.foreign_keys: 

3894 continue # a relationship-named or non-FK column is legitimate 

3895 origin, target = origin_target 

3896 ref_name = origin.__name__ 

3897 target_name = target.__name__ if target is not None else "Model" 

3898 try: 

3899 pk_name = column.type.python_type.__name__ 

3900 except Exception: 

3901 pk_name = "int" 

3902 rel = _relationship_name_for_fk(model, field_name) 

3903 rename = ( 

3904 f", or name the field `{rel}` for the {ref_name} relationship" 

3905 if rel 

3906 else "" 

3907 ) 

3908 warnings.warn( 

3909 f"{schema.__name__}.{field_name} is typed `{ref_name}[{target_name}]`, " 

3910 f"but `{field_name}` maps to the scalar foreign-key column " 

3911 f"`{model.__name__}.{field_name}`. An {ref_name} field resolves to an " 

3912 f"ORM object, so `data.{field_name}` is a reference wrapper, not the " 

3913 f"plain id. Use `{field_name}: fr.MustExist[{pk_name}, {target_name}]` " 

3914 f"for a checked scalar FK{rename}.", 

3915 RestlyMisuseWarning, 

3916 stacklevel=6, 

3917 )

3920def _model_set_fields(model: type[Any]) -> dict[str, str]: 

3921 """Map each attribute whose write sets a column that the model sets to 

3922 that column. 

3923 

3924 The model sets a column that the constructor does not take 

3925 (``init=False``) and that has a default: ``default`` or 

3926 ``default_factory`` on the field, or ``insert_default`` or 

3927 ``server_default`` on the column. A many-to-one relationship maps to its 

3928 foreign key column, because a write to the relationship sets it. A 

3929 primary key that the server generates is left out, because Restly already 

3930 leaves it out of the request bodies. 

3931 """ 

3932 if not dataclasses.is_dataclass(model): 3932 ↛ 3933line 3932 didn't jump to line 3933 because the condition on line 3932 was never true

3933 return {} 

3934 mapper = sa_inspect(model) 

3935 generated_keys = _generated_primary_key_fields(model) 

3936 columns: dict[str, str] = {} 

3937 for field in dataclasses.fields(model): 

3938 if field.init or field.name in generated_keys: 

3939 continue 

3940 column = mapper.columns.get(field.name) 

3941 if column is None: 

3942 continue 

3943 if ( 

3944 field.default is not dataclasses.MISSING 

3945 or field.default_factory is not dataclasses.MISSING 

3946 or column.default is not None 

3947 or column.server_default is not None 

3948 ): 

3949 columns[field.name] = field.name 

3950 for relationship in mapper.relationships: 

3951 for column in relationship.local_columns: 

3952 key = mapper.get_property_by_column(column).key 

3953 if key in columns: 

3954 columns[relationship.key] = key 

3955 return columns

3958def _warn_writable_model_set_fields(view_cls: type[View]) -> None: 

3959 """Flag a writable field that sets a column that the model sets. 

3960 

3961 A column with ``init=False`` and a default, such as a tenant column with

3964 builds the object, so a value in the request body replaces the default:

3968 ``schema`` already marks these columns ReadOnly.

3971 return

3983 for attr, routes in ( 

3984 ("schema_create", (ViewRoute.CREATE.value,)), 

3985 # the PUT route of a react-admin view takes the update body too 

3986 ("schema_update", (ViewRoute.UPDATE.value, "put")),

3989 continue 

3990 if not _needs_generating(view_cls, attr):

3992 elif _declared_at(view_cls, "schema") is not None: 

3993 write_classes.setdefault(view_cls.schema, True) 

3994 for cls, derived in write_classes.items(): 

3995 for field_name, field_info in cls.model_fields.items(): 

3996 column = model_set.get(field_name) 

3997 if column is None or _is_readonly(field_info): 

3998 continue 

3999 through = ( 

4000 "" 

4001 if column == field_name 

4002 else f" and sets `{model.__name__}.{column}` through the relationship" 

4003 ) 

4004 fix = ( 

4005 "Mark the field `fr.ReadOnly[...]`" 

4006 if derived 

4007 else f"Leave the field out of {cls.__name__}" 

4008 ) 

4009 warnings.warn( 

4010 f"{cls.__name__}.{field_name} is writable{through}, but " 

4011 f"`{model.__name__}.{column}` has `init=False` and a default, " 

4012 f"so the model sets it. A value in the request body replaces " 

4013 f"the default. {fix}, so the value always comes from the "
